reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's loyalty and commitment to Israel. Rahab recounts how Yahweh dried the Red Sea for Israel (v. 10) and gave them victory over the Amorite kings (v. 10). She declares 'I know that Yahweh has given you the land' (v. 9) and acknowledges 'Yahweh your God, he is God in heaven above and on earth beneath' (v. 11). The entire narrative shows Yahweh actively supporting Israel's conquest. There is no mention whatsoever of Yahweh considering replacing Israel with another people; the text emphasizes divine faithfulness and commitment to Israel's success.
